For fee-free spending abroad from the UK, Starling Bank and Chase are the best overall debit cards, while Lloyds Ultra and Barclaycard Rewards are the top credit cards. The best choice depends on whether you prefer debit (no credit checks, instant budgeting) or credit (Section 75 protection on big bookings).

Top UK Fee-Free Travel Cards Compared
Card	Type	Foreign Spending Fee	Overseas ATM Withdrawals	Key Perks & Catch
Starling Bank	Debit	0% (Mastercard rate)	Fee-free (up to £300/day, max 6/day)	Best all-rounder: No monthly ATM cap, great app, no credit check.
Chase UK	Debit	0% (Mastercard rate)	Fee-free (up to £500/day, £1,500/month)	Best for rewards: 1% cashback on everyday spending in year 1 (capped/subject to terms).
First Direct 1st Account	Debit	0% (Mastercard rate)	Fee-free (up to £500/day)	Best traditional bank: Often offers a lucrative switching bonus and top customer service.
Lloyds Ultra	Credit	0% (Visa rate)	Fee-free, but daily interest applies	Best credit card: 1% cashback worldwide in year 1 (0.25% after) + Section 75 protection.
Barclaycard Rewards	Credit	0% (Visa rate)	Fee-free & interest-free (if paid in full)	Best credit card for cash: 0.25% cashback; rare credit card with no cash advance interest.
Monzo (Free)	Debit	0% (Mastercard rate)	Free in EEA; £200/30 days outside EEA (3% after)	Great for splitting group bills and budgeting, but restrictive for cash outside Europe.
Which One Should You Pick?

For everyday spending & cash withdrawals: Go with Starling Bank. Unlike Monzo or Revolut, Starling doesn't restrict your free monthly ATM withdrawals or add weekend exchange rate markups. Chase is an equally strong alternative if you want cashback and don't need more than £1,500/month in foreign cash.

+ 1

For hotels, flights, and car hire: Use a fee-free credit card like Lloyds Ultra or Barclaycard Rewards. Paying by credit card gives you Section 75 protection on purchases between £100 and £30,000 if a company goes bust or something goes wrong—and car rental desks strongly prefer credit cards for security deposits. (Always set up a Direct Debit to pay the balance in full each month to avoid high APR interest.)   
Money Saving Expert
+ 1

If you don't want a new bank account: Trading 212 (free Invest account, no investing required) offers a Mastercard debit card with 0% fees and the pure interbank exchange rate, though free ATM withdrawals are capped at £400/month.

Golden Rule When Paying Abroad

Always choose to pay in the local currency (e.g., Euros, Dollars) on card machines and ATMs. If you select GBP (£), the merchant or ATM uses Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) and applies their own terrible exchange rate, wiping out your card's fee-free benefit.

Are you planning a specific trip where you'll need lots of cash, or mostly paying by card?
